Wonty Support

Need help, found a bug, or want to report something? Write to us at krasovskyi.yevhenii@gmail.com.

Tell us what happened, what you expected, your iPhone model and iOS version, and the Wonty version (Settings > About Wonty). Screenshots help a lot. If your question is about your account, write from the email address you use in Wonty, or tell us which one it is.

Frequently asked questions

What is Wonty?

Wonty keeps everything you wish for in one place: gifts, trips, dinners and experiences. Save a wish from any shop or website, group your wishes into catalogs for every occasion, and share them with friends and family. They can reserve a gift without spoiling the surprise, so nothing gets bought twice. You can also organize events, such as a birthday or a Secret Santa with a secret draw.

Do I need an account?

No. Without an account, you can keep wishes and catalogs on your phone, and everything you create stays there.

An account lets you back up your wishes, sync them across your devices, share catalogs, join events and reserve gifts. When you sign in for the first time, the wishes and catalogs already on your phone are added to your account.

How do I sign in?

Open Settings and tap Sign In. Depending on your device, you can choose:

  • Sign in with Apple: confirm with Face ID, Touch ID or your passcode;
  • Continue with Google: choose your Google account;
  • Email: enter your email address, and we email you a 6-digit code. There is no password.

If you sign in with Apple or Google using the same email address as your Wonty account, you reach the same account. If you chose "Hide My Email" with Apple, your account uses an Apple relay address, so keep signing in with Apple: signing in with your real email address would create a separate account.

I didn't get the sign-in code

  • Check that the email address is spelled correctly. If not, tap Use a different email.
  • Look in your spam or junk folder, and in other tabs or folders your email app may use.
  • Wait a minute, then tap Send a new code. The button shows when you can ask again.
  • The code works for 10 minutes. If it has expired, ask for a new one.
  • If you see "Too many attempts", wait a little before trying again.
  • Work and school email systems sometimes hold back automated emails. Try another address, or sign in with Apple or Google.

Still stuck? Write to krasovskyi.yevhenii@gmail.com and tell us the address you tried.

How do I share a list with someone?

Lists in Wonty are called catalogs.

  1. Open the catalog and tap Share catalog. If you haven't yet, Wonty asks you to sign in and to add your name, so friends know who you are.
  2. Send the link by message, email or any app, or copy it.
  3. Your friend opens the link, signs in (and adds a name, if they haven't yet), and can then see the catalog and reserve gifts from it.

Anyone who has the link and signs in can join, so send it only to people you want to see the catalog. In the share screen you can see who joined, remove people, and reset the link so the old one stops working. Your friends see the wishes in that catalog, never your other wishes.

How do I invite friends to an event?

Open the event and tap Invite people, then send the link, or tap Copy link. Anyone who has the link and signs in can join while the list is open, so send it only to people you want in the event. You can reset the link (Reset invite link) so the old one stops working; people who already joined stay in.

What your friend does next:

  • If they have Wonty: tap the link, and Wonty opens the invitation. If a web page opens instead, tap Open in Wonty there.
  • If they don't have Wonty yet:
    1. Tap the link, then Get Wonty. The page copies the invitation and opens the App Store.
    2. Install Wonty and open it.
    3. Right away, on the welcome screen, Wonty offers to open the invitation they copied. They tap Paste; the invitation opens once they tap Get Started (or sign in). Wonty reads the clipboard only when Paste is tapped.
    4. If that offer doesn't appear (for example, because something else was copied in the meantime), just tap the invitation link again: now that Wonty is installed, it opens the invitation.
  • Then: sign in (or create an account) to see the invitation, and tap Join.

How do gift reservations work, and who can see them?

When you open a catalog someone shared with you, or a wishlist in an event, tap Reserve on the gift you plan to buy. Others then see that it's taken, so nobody buys the same thing. You can mark it as purchased or cancel the reservation at any time. All your reservations are in the Gifting tab.

What the person who made the wish sees depends on the setting they chose for the catalog:

  • Keep it a surprise (the default): nothing at all;
  • Show what is reserved: that the wish is reserved, but not by whom;
  • Show who reserved: who reserved it, and whether it was bought.

In a Secret Santa event, the person you're giving to never sees your reservation, whatever their setting.

Wonty shows you what the owner will see before you reserve. Other people who share the catalog with you can see your name next to your reservation. In a Secret Santa event, nobody else sees that the reservation is yours.

You can choose what you see about reservations on your own catalogs when you edit a catalog, under What you see about reservations.

How does Secret Santa work?

  1. Create an event with the Secret Santa type. Set a budget and a date if you like, and invite your group.
  2. Everyone joins and can add a wishlist, so their Secret Santa knows what they'd like. Only the person who draws them will see it.
  3. When everyone is in, the organizer taps Lock the list, then Draw names. At least three people are needed.
  4. Each person sees only who they give a gift to, and can open that person's wishlist and reserve a gift there in secret. Nobody else, not even the organizer, can see who drew whom in the app.

With exactly three people, everyone can work out all the pairs, and Wonty warns you about this before the draw. If someone leaves after the draw, their person usually goes to whoever was giving to them; otherwise the organizer is asked to redo the draw. If the organizer redoes the draw, the reservations made in the event are cancelled and names are drawn again. If names can't be drawn yet (for example, because fewer than three people are left), the draw is only reset, and the organizer can draw names later.

How do I delete my account and my data?

Go to Settings > Account > Delete Account and confirm. If you use Sign in with Apple, Apple asks you to confirm too. This permanently deletes your account, your wishes, catalogs, pictures and reservations, from our servers and from your phone. It can't be undone. Events you organized that other people are still part of are handed over to another participant.

  • Sign Out is different: it removes your data from that phone only, and it comes back when you sign in again.
  • Without an account, your data is only on your phone. Deleting a wish or catalog removes it from the app; to remove everything, including hidden records of deleted items, delete the app.
  • You can also ask us to delete your account by writing to krasovskyi.yevhenii@gmail.com from your account's email address.

Our Privacy Policy explains what is deleted and what remains for a limited time.

How do I report abusive content or a user?

In the app, tap Report: on a friend's wish, in the menu of a catalog shared with you or of an event you joined, or next to a person in an event. Wonty opens your email app with a message to us. Say what's wrong in your own words, and keep the lines at the end: they tell us what you are reporting (the IDs of the catalog, wish, event or person, and your own user ID). Nothing is sent until you send the email.

Or write to krasovskyi.yevhenii@gmail.com with:

  • what happened;
  • the name the person uses in Wonty, and the name of the catalog or event;
  • screenshots, if you can.

We review every report and can remove content or close accounts that are used for abuse.

You can also act right away:

  • leave a catalog or an event you don't want to be part of (Leave event for events);
  • if it's your catalog, remove the person and reset the share link;
  • if you organize the event, remove the person (Remove from event) and reset the invite link.

If someone is in immediate danger, contact your local emergency services.

Where can I read about privacy?

In our Privacy Policy. In short: there are no ads, no analytics and no tracking, and you can use Wonty without an account.
